title: Sephiria Wishing Fountain — Town Artifact Picker
description: Sephiria wishing fountain guide: unlock via Destiny New Events, pick town Artifacts for the next run, and how Willpower expands capacity.
meta: Town pre-run Artifact picker; capacity figures are community-reported and should be checked in-game, and picks are best confirmed after the weapon family is chosen.
sources: YT: intro tips (wishing well / artifact favorites)
body:
The Sephiria Wishing Fountain in town is easy to miss: it is a pre-run Artifact picker, not the dungeon interactable whose water changes color.

The same object is also searched as the “fountain of wishes” or the wishing well — all three point to the town Artifact picker described below.

What it does

Once unlocked, you select Artifacts in Bunnyville and carry those picks into the next dungeon run. Intro footage treats this as the “wishing well” step after you decide a weapon / combo family.

That ordering is the whole point of the object. The fountain sits before the floor loads, and nothing in the sources here describes a way to change a pick once the run has started — so a pick confirmed for the wrong family is not a mistake you repair inside the dungeon. It is capacity spent for the length of the run.

Confirm the picks only after that family is chosen. A summoner start spends the slots on Companion-tagged Artifacts — the Companion build is the pick list. Higher rarity is reported to cost more of the bar, so one expensive Artifact can use up the default capacity of 4 and leave the rest of the set for the dungeon.

Do not mix this up with in-dungeon fountains that can grant XP, gold, or spawn enemies when the water changes color. Those are a different object.

How you unlock it

Open it through New Events on Destiny Inscription—the same early spends that unlock the costume salon and extra weapons. See the beginner guide.

The unlock is not free, and it competes for the same currency as everything else on that board. Sapphires are recorded as coming from dungeon depth and bosses defeated, so the New Events line that opens the fountain is spending Sapphires that weapon training also wants. The Destiny Inscription page puts New Events first in its early spend order, ahead of Home Repairs and ahead of weapon training, and that is the order that reaches the fountain soonest.

There is a second gap worth knowing before you plan around capacity. Willpower is listed among the talents, and talents are recorded as opening after Home Repairs. A fresh save therefore reaches the picker at the default capacity and only earns the extra bars later, once the Home Repairs line has opened the talent screen and Willpower has levels in it. Read the default four as the number you start with, not as the number you finish on.

Order of operations before a run

  1. Choose the weapon family first. The weapons page lists the six branches and what each is good at. A run cannot be planned around a branch the save has not unlocked.
  2. Check what is actually unlocked. Nothing you have not unlocked will appear on the pick screen, so read the Journal before walking to the fountain.
  3. Confirm the picks. Match them to the family from step one, not to the rarest line on the list.
  4. Check the active inventory. A pick that ends up in the Side Bag is inactive, and the Side Bag rule applies to Artifacts as much as to Tablets.
  5. Start the run. Everything after this point happens inside the dungeon: shop stock, boss rewards, adjacency reshuffles.
Steps one and two are the easiest to skip, because the fountain screen shows what you are allowed to take, not what your run can use. Those are different questions, and only the first one is answered in town.

Capacity

  • A community talent writeup reports a default capacity of 4; verify the current value in-game.
  • Willpower expands it: +1 at talent Lv5 and +4 at Lv20, for a reported maximum of 9; verify this against your current talent levels. A 1.0 tips video also treats Willpower as the stat that changes fountain / dice quality.
  • A community writeup reports that higher rarity costs more capacity (Common 3 / Advanced 4 / Rare 5 / Legendary 6). Confirm the current bars in-client; these figures may have changed.

What the reported numbers add up to

Both halves of the capacity question are community-reported, so the honest use for them is shape rather than precision. Set side by side, the reported rarity costs land like this:

RarityReported costAgainst the reported default of 4Against the reported maximum of 9
Common3Fits, one point left overFits, six left over
Advanced4Fills the bar exactlyFits, five left over
Rare5Exceeds the defaultFits, four left over
Legendary6Exceeds the defaultFits, three left over

Costs and capacities both come from the community writeups cited on this page, checked 9 November 2026. They do not sit comfortably together: at a default of 4 a Rare could not be carried at all, and a single Common leaves one point that nothing else can use. The likeliest explanation is that the two numbers were recorded at different talent levels or on different saves. Read the table for the shape — cheap items fit several picks, expensive items eat the bar — and read the real numbers off your own fountain screen.

At the reported maximum the arithmetic does compose: three Commons, an Advanced with a Rare, or a Legendary with a Common all land on 9 exactly. That is the one point where planning a full set is worth the effort. Below it the practical rule is one pick that matters plus whatever else fits, rather than a symmetric set the bar cannot hold.

Choosing picks for a build family

Much of this decision is made before you reach the fountain. The fountain is the last step of a plan that begins on the weapons page, and the builds overview is where the families are described. Both the Companion build page and this one put the same step first: settle the weapon and combo family, then load the picks that support it.

For a summoner start the answer is already written out. The companion route wants Companion-tagged items early — contracts, moles, jellyfish, cushions and similar summon pieces — and the Companion build page makes pre-loading those fountain picks the second item in its first-floor checklist. For any other family the constraint is the beginner guide rule: commit to one or two combo tags and let the fountain serve those two, rather than taking one pick per tag in the hope that something switches on.

What the fountain will not do is supply the pieces that need two tags at once. The builds page records a Steam discussion reporting that Bond Artifacts are not offered there, which is why the bond set documented on the Artifacts page has to be assembled inside the run. Plan the fountain around single-tag pieces and treat any bond as a dungeon problem, not a town one.

Situation at the fountainWhat to doWhy
Family not chosen yetLeave and choose firstPicks are pre-run, so a wrong-family pick costs capacity for the whole run
A Rare or Legendary is the only thing on offerAssume it may fill the bar by itselfReported costs of 5 and 6 against a reported default of 4
Only Commons on offerTake one and expect a wasted pointAt a bar of 4 a Common leaves a single point that nothing can use
A Bond Artifact is what the plan needsDo not expect it hereA Steam discussion recorded on the builds page reports bonds are not offered at the fountain
Picks look right but the run feels emptyCheck the Side BagStored items are inactive, so a pick can be owned and doing nothing

The first row is the ordering rule this page argues for; rows two and three follow from the reported capacity figures; the last two from the linked pages. None of it replaces reading the picker in your own client.

If you confirm before the family is chosen

The failure is quiet, which is why it repeats. Nothing errors: the picks are accepted, the run starts, and the Artifacts sit in the inventory contributing less than they would inside the family they were built for. The player then blames the drop pool, when the actual mistake happened in town two screens earlier.

There is a second version of the same mistake — choosing a family, taking picks for it, then abandoning the plan on the first floor because a shop offered something shinier. The fountain did its job; the run did not. If a run has to change direction, change it before the next fountain visit rather than after the picks are already spent.

Common mistakes

  • Picking the rarest Artifact on the list. Rarity is the cost, not the fit. A Legendary that supports nothing in the run is an expensive empty slot.
  • Filling the bar with one pick. A single expensive Artifact can consume the reported default capacity, which leaves the run with one effect instead of a set.
  • Picking for a family that is not unlocked. The screen only shows what your save has, so the plan has to match the save, not a video.
  • Expecting bonds. They are reported as not offered at the fountain, so a plan that starts with one starts broken.
  • Leaving the picks in the Side Bag. Inactive means inactive; the fountain does not care where an item ends up after you take it.
  • Treating the default as the maximum. Four is where a save starts. Willpower moves it, and that talent route opens later than the fountain does.

What this page does not cover

  • Which Artifact to keep and where to place it. Slot decisions, adjacency and bond pairs are on the Artifacts and Tablets page.
  • Which family to pick. The six branches and their tradeoffs are on weapons; finished routes are on builds.
  • How to afford the unlock. Sapphire sources and the spend order are on Destiny Inscription.
  • What prepared starts are worth at higher difficulty. Hard Mode is where they matter most.

Quick FAQ

Is the Wishing Fountain the same as the fountain in the dungeon?

No. The town object is a pre-run Artifact picker. The dungeon interactable is the one whose water changes color and can grant XP, gold, or spawn enemies.

Do I need it before my first run?

You can play without it. It opens through New Events on Destiny Inscription, which the Destiny page puts first in its early spend order — so it is usually an early unlock rather than a late one.

How many Artifacts can I take?

A community writeup reports a default of 4, expanded by Willpower to a reported maximum of 9. Verify both in your client, because the reported per-rarity costs do not fit a bar of 4 cleanly.

Does rarity matter more than fit?

Fit first. Higher rarity is reported to cost more capacity, so an expensive pick can use the entire default bar and leave the run with a single effect.

Can I take a Bond Artifact from the fountain?

A Steam discussion recorded on the builds page reports that bonds are not offered there. Treat them as in-run finds and keep the fountain for single-tag pieces.

When exactly should I confirm?

After the weapon and combo family for that run is chosen, and before the floor loads. Nothing in the sources cited here documents a way to change the picks once the run begins.

For optional dungeon rewards after a run begins, see how to find Sephiria secret rooms. Related: Companion build (start with the Companion family) · Destiny / talents · Artifacts · Builds.

Picking Artifacts only pays off if they are actually active in your run: items in the Side Bag stay inactive, including Tablets. During a run, secret-room cracks are a separate source of supplies.
